item.title: Fans look forward to Mataeles impresseive try scoring spree in white jersey
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians winger Manasa Mataele will try and continue his try-scoring spree in the white jersey, exciting the Drua faithful throughout his debut season and earning him the title of Tropik Wood Industries Limited Fan Player of the Year . This was shared by fans from Lautoka with fijivillage News today.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians winger Manasa Mataele will try and continue his try-scoring spree in the white jersey, exciting the Drua faithful throughout his debut season and earning him the title of Tropik Wood Industries Limited Fan Player of the Year .

This was shared by fans from Lautoka with fijivillage News today.

Mataele scored 6 tries in his first season with the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua.

He scooped the Tropik Wood Fan Player of the Year Award last season with the Drua and captured the imagination and admiration of the Drua Nation through his performances and connection with the fans.

Mataele’s electric performances and attacking flair made him a clear favourite among the Drua faithful, as he wrapped up his first season with the club with an impressive six tries .

The Flying Fijians will face Canada this Saturday at 7pm.

item.title: 7-year wait over as Nasinu book BOG semi-final showdown with Rewa
item.description: Nasinu FC President Jagindar Singh says qualifying for the Extra Battle of the Giants semi-finals for the first time in seven years is a proud achievement for the Giant Killers. Fiji Football Association says Nasinu entered the tournament as underdogs and without a major sponsor but finished second in Group A following victories over Blue Gas Navua FC and Global Care Suva FC.
item.content:encoded:
Nasinu FC President Jagindar Singh says qualifying for the Extra Battle of the Giants semi-finals for the first time in seven years is a proud achievement for the Giant Killers.

Fiji Football Association says Nasinu entered the tournament as underdogs and without a major sponsor but finished second in Group A following victories over Blue Gas Navua FC and Global Care Suva FC.

The side suffered a narrow 1-0 loss to defending champions Extra Supermarket Labasa FC in its opening match before bouncing back to defeat Navua 1-0.

Nasinu then secured its place in the semi-finals with an impressive 2-1 win over Suva in its final pool match.

Singh says the achievement reflects the commitment and sacrifices made by the players, officials and supporters.

He says they came into the tournament as underdogs, and he is proud of what the players and officials have achieved.

Singh says the side does not have a major sponsor, but everyone involved has worked hard and made sacrifices for Nasinu.

He adds that qualifying for the semi-finals is the best Father’s Day gift for all the fathers and supporters of Nasinu.

Fiji FA says under coach Abunesh Kapoor, Nasinu has displayed discipline and determination throughout the competition.

Nasinu last reached the BOG semi-finals in 2019, when the side held Labasa scoreless for 90 minutes before losing 3-0 in extra time.

The Giant Killers have finished runners-up twice, in 1989 and 1991, but are yet to win the tournament.

Nasinu will now face Group B winner Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC in the second semi-final at 4.30pm this Saturday at the Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: Pita Naidrolevu appointed Tailevu Rugby Men’s Senior Team Manager
item.description: Pita Naidrolevu has been appointed the new Tailevu Rugby Men’s Senior Team Manager, taking over the role previously held by the late Wame Bainivanua. The Tailevu Rugby Football Union says Naidrolevu was appointed to the position by its Executive Committee as the Union continues preparations and development of its senior men’s team.
item.content:encoded:
Pita Naidrolevu has been appointed the new Tailevu Rugby Men’s Senior Team Manager, taking over the role previously held by the late Wame Bainivanua.

The Tailevu Rugby Football Union says Naidrolevu was appointed to the position by its Executive Committee as the Union continues preparations and development of its senior men’s team.

The Union says Naidrolevu takes on the responsibility with its trust and confidence and will work closely with the players, coaching panel, management and supporters.

It says his appointment also marks a new chapter for the senior team as he continues the work and legacy established by the late Bainivanua.

Tailevu Rugby says Bainivanua’s dedication, service and commitment to the Union left a lasting mark and will always be remembered and respected.

The Union says it is confident Naidrolevu will carry forward the same spirit of service and teamwork as he takes on his new role.

It has congratulated Naidrolevu on his appointment and wished him success as he leads the team with commitment, humility, unity and purpose.

item.title: OFC U-19 Men’s Championship: Junior Bula Boys turn focus to must-win Tahiti clash
item.description: The Junior Bula Boys face a crucial final pool match against Tahiti tomorrow as they push for a place in the semi-finals of the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship. Midfielder Maikah Dau says the team will learn from its mistakes against New Zealand and come back stronger for the Tahiti match.
item.content:encoded:
The Junior Bula Boys face a crucial final pool match against Tahiti tomorrow as they push for a place in the semi-finals of the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship.

Midfielder Maikah Dau says the team will learn from its mistakes against New Zealand and come back stronger for the Tahiti match.

The U-19 team went down 2-nil to New Zealand in their second pool match.

Dau says there is a lot to learn from the New Zealand match, particularly after the Junior Bula Boys held their opponents scoreless in the first half.

He says the team lacked some adaptation and focus after the break but will learn from its mistakes ahead of the Tahiti match.

He says the players will follow the coach’s instructions as they prepare for their final group match.

Meanwhile, defender Farhaan Khan says although the result against New Zealand did not go their way, the team now knows what it needs to improve.

Khan says the team will work on its weaknesses before coming back stronger against Tahiti.

He says he is proud of the players for their effort and the way they supported each other throughout the match.

Both players have thanked supporters, fans and parents for their continued support and prayers.

Fiji will face Tahiti in their final pool match tomorrow at 10am at the Samoa Football HQ in Apia , while New Zealand, who have already booked a place in the semi-finals, will face Vanuatu at 2pm.

item.title: OFC U-16 Women’s Championship: Mini Kulas thrash Cook Islands 11-0
item.description: Fiji’s Mini Kulas have made a stunning start to the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship after thrashing the Cook Islands 11-0 in Honiara, Solomon Islands. Adi Reva was the star of the match, scoring five goals as Fiji dominated from the opening whistle.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s Mini Kulas have made a stunning start to the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship after thrashing the Cook Islands 11-0 in Honiara, Solomon Islands.

Adi Reva was the star of the match, scoring five goals as Fiji dominated from the opening whistle.

Torika Boseiwaqa opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the fifth minute before adding her second in the 26th minute.

Esther Vunivi also scored before Reva began her five-goal haul with two goals before half-time.

Reva completed her hat-trick in the 50th minute before adding two more goals late in the match.

Temalesi Masi scored twice after coming off the bench, while Elisha Narayan completed the scoring with the final kick of the game.

The result is Fiji’s biggest-ever win at the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship, with Reva also becoming the first Fijian player to score five goals in a single match at the tournament.

Head coach Nicola Demaine praised the performance but urged her players to remain focused on their next match.

Demaine says the team must not get carried away despite the impressive opening result.

Fiji will next face New Zealand on Wednesday at 5pm before taking on the Solomon Islands next Saturday at 8pm.

The semi-finals will be played on 16th September, with the final scheduled for 19th September.

The winner and the runner-up will qualify for FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2027.

item.title: La Liga: Yamal scores twice as Barcelona thrash Valencia 5-0
item.description: Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona continued their impressive start to the La Liga season with a 5-0 win over Valencia. Yamal opened the scoring in the sixth minute before Fermín López doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 22nd minute.
item.content:encoded:
Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona continued their impressive start to the La Liga season with a 5-0 win over Valencia.

Yamal opened the scoring in the sixth minute before Fermín López doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 22nd minute.

Raphinha made it 3-0 shortly after the break, with Pedri adding Barcelona’s fourth in the 79th minute.

Yamal completed the scoring with his second goal of the match in the 84th minute.

Barcelona have now scored 17 goals in four matches and conceded just two.

Valencia remain bottom with just one point from their opening four games.

Meanwhile, Alavés thrashed Osasuna 5-2, while Málaga and Levante played out a goalless draw.

Espanyol and Sevilla also settled for a 1-all draw.
